t: You're on Hatton Garden, a shopping street in Holborn and London's main diamond and jewellery quarter, on the edge of the West End. The name comes from Sir Christopher Hatton, a favourite of Elizabeth the First who became Lord Chancellor. He was one of the judges who found Mary, Queen of Scots guilty of treason. Others connected with the street include the engraver Charles Taylor and the German-born bookseller and translator John de Verdion, who both died here. The lithographer William West and the customs commissioner John Manley lived here.
